model_proposal.rationale: H2 and H4 both indicate that perception errors and grasp variability cause missed grasps and slips. The one-at-a-time effect shows retry_count 0->3 boosted overall pass rate from 70% to 81%. This single-parameter change isolates the retry benefit without altering other dynamics.
model_proposal.expected_effect: Reduce MISSED_GRASP in high sensor noise / negative pos_offset_y region (H2) and reduce SLIPPED_ON_LIFT and MISSED_GRASP in low friction / high sensor noise region (H4). Overall pass rate should increase significantly.

model_proposal.rationale: H1 requires higher grip_force for heavy low-friction cubes; H4 also benefits from both grip_force and retry_count. Slowing lift_speed reduces inertial load during lift, which helps both H1 (slip during lift) and H4 (slip threshold). This three-parameter combo attacks multiple failure modes simultaneously.
model_proposal.expected_effect: Reduce MISSED_GRASP and SLIPPED_ON_LIFT in heavy low-friction region (H1) and low-friction high-noise region (H4). Slower lift should also help small cubes with high gripper delay (H3) by reducing inertial disturbance after grasp.

model_proposal.rationale: H3 suggests small cubes with high gripper_delay_steps need more time for grasp to stabilize; maxing grasp_hold_steps gives the largest possible wait. H1 and H4 both benefit from higher grip_force; using the max (80 N) is a large step to see if the slip threshold can be raised enough to eliminate slips in the worst-case region.
model_proposal.expected_effect: Drastically reduce MISSED_GRASP and COLLISION in small-cube high-delay region (H3). Maximize friction capacity to eliminate SLIPPED_ON_LIFT in heavy low-friction (H1) and low-friction high-noise (H4) regions. Risk: very high grip_force may cause excessive finger forces but should stay within motor limits.

model_proposal.rationale: Conservative multi-parameter nudge: each parameter moves a small step in the direction suggested by hypotheses. This tests whether modest, balanced adjustments can improve pass rate without risking side effects (e.g., too-slow lift increasing cycle time, too-high grip_force causing wear).
model_proposal.expected_effect: Slight improvements across all hypotheses: H1 (grip_force +10 N), H2 (retry_count +1), H3 (grasp_hold_steps +20), H4 (grip_force +10 N, retry_count +1). Lift speed reduction from 0.3 to 0.25 m/s marginally lowers inertial load. Overall pass rate should edge up without regressions.
